r4-m10-rival.rival: Early RL-Zero-Math adopts the RL opening and lengthens deliberation at once (step 100 is the cued base in format, length and per-token sharpness), but 3.1's truncation-as-negative reward starts pruning the T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 loop hazard from the first steps rather than late, so cap hits fall steadily in log-steps (cued base ~0.24 -> step 100 ~0.19 -> step 400 ~0.15 -> step 2,800 ~0.03) instead of sitting flat at the cued-base level through step 400.

rows.experiment: Cap-hit rate of RL step 400, plain prompt, MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
rows.theory_should_say: The theory has cap hits at the cued-base level (119/500 ~ 0.24) at step 100, flat through step 400, so it implies ~0.22-0.24; the rival has early truncation-negative pruning already bringing it to ~0.15.

rows.experiment: Paired change in cap-hit rate from RL step 100 to RL step 400, plain prompt, MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 (step 100 minus step 400).
rows.theory_should_say: The theory says cap hits stay flat from step 100 to step 400 (only later commit-and-stop training removes them), so it implies ~0.00; the rival has them falling steadily, so ~+0.05.

rows.experiment: Paired cap-hit rate difference on the 400-problem harder set at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95: RL step 400 plain minus cued base.
rows.theory_should_say: The theory says step 400 loops exactly like the cued base (the cue-forced deliberation mode, not yet pruned), so it implies ~0.00 (or slightly positive from longer chains); the rival has loop pruning already under way, giving ~-0.10 on the cap-heavy hard set (cued base ~0.5 cap hits there).
